- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in the history.
- Model underestimates late-period prices (last 5–10 days) — shows mean reversion bias, failing to capture sustained upward momentum.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 10 days, suggesting lag or delayed response to recent price trends.
- Model fails to capture the “tail” of the price curve — true outcomes often rise faster and higher than forecasted in the final 10–15 days.
- Overconfidence in short-term momentum leads to overestimation of volatility or upward drift.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to adjust downward when recent history shows downward pressure, even if it’s a short-term correction.
- Forecasts should be calibrated to reflect recent mean reversion, especially when history shows a clear trend reversal.
- Avoid overfitting to recent spikes — model should dampen overreaction to single-day or short-term volatility.
- Use a moving average or exponential smoothing filter to reduce overshoot and lag in forecasts.
